scope: Nine reviewed central case documents plus six navigation pointers; not all project history or private app docs.
transport: MCP only; existing gateway authentication; no model-provider credentials
profile: chunks-only retain, no observations/auto consolidation, no temporal/graph/reranking stages, no reflect or generated pages
update_policy: Explicit reviewed apply only. Verify source hashes before writing; replace stable document IDs. No automatic install-time ingestion.

entries.probe: Downloads work on a laptop but scheduled server reports are stale. How do we verify source freshness and dependent report recovery?
Refund credits become positive purchases and a preference bonus changes cash totals. Which calculation and comparison mistakes should we avoid?
A provider may have accepted a request before timeout and listing fails. How should durable intent and reconciliation work?
The dashboard health check passes but the browser receives a truncated JavaScript plugin through the proxy. What should we investigate?
A storage-based database cost estimate missed tiny inserts, merge work and write amplification. How do we review cost assumptions and runtime drift?
The native metronome passes helper tests but produces no audible clicks. What acceptance evidence is still required?
One rescued video demo passed but fresh unattended drafts still fail at asset recognition and provider refusal. Is automation ready?
An unchanged app revision uses a changed shared container build recipe. How do we identify the exact artifact to promote?
After extracting a page, its GET works but the first browser save returns 404. What gateway and mutation-route test did the mock miss?

entries.summary: Historical cross-project engineering cases are indexed in docs/case-studies/README.md. It routes to Panyora extraction and CI/CD, Elvique operational UX and observability, Servinoza workflow recovery and extraction, NarrateAI unattended automation, bulkBuyer provenance, DelX durable execution, card-savvy calculations, infrastructure cost/drift and native audio acceptance. Choose by failure mechanism, read each case and its linked skills, preserve evidence limits and decide adopt/adapt/reject. These are historical cases, not current app architecture. Current owner pointers are in docs/PROJECT_CATALOG.md; remaining review backlog is in docs/LEARNING_COVERAGE.md.
entries.probe: Where is the index of historical engineering mistakes across our different projects?

entries.summary: Current project architecture, cron and worker ownership, CI/CD, deployment and operational documentation are located through docs/PROJECT_CATALOG.md. Resolve the named owner's repository and owner-relative path within authorized access. Panyora uses panyora-docs and panyora-ops. Servinoza uses servinoza-docs for the current migration record, servinoza-ops for container CI/runtime and servinoza-db-ops for database operations; the former Servinoza_in parent is retired historical source rather than a current runtime dependency. The catalog also points to Elvique, NarrateAI, bulkBuyer, DelX and card-savvy docs. Reopen current owner files, check revision and running-state evidence; dated baselines and successful image promotion do not certify later releases, provider money movement or every workflow. Do not automatically clone private sources or assume sibling access. Central refresh does not refresh app checkouts.
entries.probe: Where do I find existing projects' current architecture, cron ownership, CI/CD and operational documentation?

entries.summary: Use docs/REUSABLE_ENGINEERING_PLAYBOOK.md to route engineering work to maintained skills and specialist roles. custom/skills/service-architecture-and-extraction/SKILL.md covers boundaries and staged extraction; custom/skills/reliable-web-app-operations/SKILL.md covers CI/CD, container builds, releases, database recovery, telemetry and provider delivery; custom/skills/api-docs-governance/SKILL.md covers contracts, discovery and document lifecycle; custom/skills/build-usable-apps/SKILL.md covers operational UI; custom/skills/auditable-business-workflows/SKILL.md covers money, transitions and historical evidence; custom/skills/sre-incident-investigation/SKILL.md covers active causal investigation. Classify docs as current, retained evidence, superseded or duplicate; validate tracked cross-repository links after moves. Read linked references selectively. manifest.json selects provider-owned agents and revisions; installation is not invocation or authorization. Preserve original providers, do not duplicate their agent libraries. Central cases supply evidence and application docs remain with their owners.
entries.probe: Which shared skills and specialist roles should I select for service extraction, CI/CD, security, database recovery and operational user interfaces?

entries.summary: Follow docs/LEARNING_WORKFLOW.md after a meaningful failure, correction, migration, switch or release. Update current application docs and retain accepted ADRs or release/incident/recovery evidence when they still support a decision, claim, audit or restoration path. Remove a superseded transition diary from the current tree when its facts have a canonical owner, it has no active recovery/compliance use, Git retains history and inbound links are repaired. Search by topic/project, use ai-setup library to locate the canonical checkout, and amend the existing central case/skill with problem, attempted approach, observed result, reason for switching, replacement/status, verification limits, reuse gate and source revision/hash/date. Preserve reusable superseded reasoning with successor pointers. Sanitize private context; use a private authorized destination when needed. If central writes are out of scope, report pending promotion. Reviewed Hindsight memory is secondary to canonical files, and Git publication and other-machine refresh require their normal authorization. No automatic transcript capture, guaranteed compliance or model retraining is implied.
entries.probe: After a failed approach and a verified fix, where should the reasoning be captured so another project does not repeat the mistake?

entries.summary: Use docs/HINDSIGHT.md for the shared Hindsight MCP setup and verification workflow. Hindsight is a semantic discovery layer over reviewed central files; Git remains canonical and client models perform reasoning. Use the shared-project-learnings bank through the configured MCP, preserve the chunks-only profile, and avoid reflect, generated pages, direct REST calls and model-provider credentials. For Codex, bearer_token_env_var must be the environment-variable name LLM_GATEWAY_KEY, with the value available in the newly started client process. Retain only reviewed sanitized entries with stable document IDs, source paths, hashes, revisions, dates and evidence limits; replace changed entries deliberately, read them back and test recall. There is no background synchronization, automatic transcript ingestion or guaranteed recall.
entries.probe: How should Claude or Codex configure, verify and safely maintain our shared Hindsight memory without a server-side model key?

entries.summary: Use docs/GLOBAL_SKILLS.md for shared skill ownership and client discovery. Installed skills are under ~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md; Claude links under ~/.claude/skills and Codex discovers the shared catalog. Canonical custom skills are in custom/skills/; custom/skills/README.md catalogs them. manifest.json identifies original providers and pinned revisions for third-party skills and agent roles; fetch them from their providers rather than caching their payloads in ai_setup or Hindsight. Read the engineering playbook to select relevant skills/roles, and reload a stale client catalog when needed. App-specific architecture, policies, runbooks, discussions and test evidence stay with the app. Global availability means the current OS user's supported clients can discover skills; it does not make every tool/application worker execute them. Historical migration counts are dated; inspect the current manifest and installed catalog.
entries.probe: Where are reusable skills and agents maintained and how can existing or new projects use the same global library?
